Season.how_to_read: Label only; no good or bad direction.

Player.tooltip: Player name. Players are tracked by ID, so players who share a name stay separate.
Player.how_to_read: Label only; no good or bad direction.

Team.tooltip: Team abbreviation. Traded players show their final team.
Team.how_to_read: Label only; no good or bad direction.

Pos.how_to_read: Context only; no good or bad direction.

Age.how_to_read: Context only; no good or bad direction.

GP.how_to_read: Volume, not quality. Useful for hiding small samples.

MP.how_to_read: Volume, not quality. Useful for hiding small samples.

Score.tooltip: One overall impact number for the season, combining several public impact models. 0 is league average.
Score.glossary: One season-long rating of a player's overall impact. It blends several respected public impact models. 0 is league average; in the playoffs, 0 is the average playoff player.
Score.how_to_read: Higher is better. Above 0 means above-average impact; below 0 means below average.

O-Score.tooltip: The offensive part of Impact Aggregate: how much the player helps the team score. 0 is league average.
O-Score.glossary: The offense-only version of Impact Aggregate: how much the player adds to the team's scoring, measured against the league with 0 as average. Read it next to D-Impact Aggregate to see which end of the floor drives a player's value.
O-Score.how_to_read: Higher is better. Above 0 means above-average offensive impact.

D-Score.tooltip: The defensive part of Impact Aggregate: how much the player helps the team defend. 0 is league average.
D-Score.glossary: The defense-only version of Impact Aggregate: how much the player adds to the team's defense, measured against the league with 0 as average. Positive values mean better defense, so no sign flip is needed when comparing with the offensive column.
D-Score.how_to_read: Higher is better. Above 0 means above-average defensive impact.

mpPPP.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the team's net points per 100 possessions with the player on the floor. Higher is better.
mpPPP.glossary: RAPM estimates a player's effect on the scoreboard while accounting for the other nine players on the floor. This is the one-year version for overall margin (offense minus defense), in points per 100 possessions.
mpPPP.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means the team outscores opponents by more with the player on the floor.

mpoPPP.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the points the team scores per 100 possessions with the player on the floor. Higher is better.
mpoPPP.glossary: The offensive side of the one-year RAPM scoring estimate: how many more points per 100 possessions the team scores with the player on the floor, after accounting for teammates and opponents. Compare it with oTS% and oTOV% to see where the gain comes from.
mpoPPP.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means the offense scores more with the player on the floor.

mpdPPP.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the points opponents score per 100 possessions with the player on the floor. Lower is better.
mpdPPP.glossary: The defensive side of the one-year RAPM scoring estimate: how many points per 100 possessions the opponents score with the player on the floor, after accounting for teammates and opponents. Negative values mark good defenders.
mpdPPP.how_to_read: Lower is better. Negative means opponents score less with the player on the floor.

mpoTS%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the team's true shooting % with the player on the floor, in points. Higher is better.
mpoTS%.glossary: The one-year RAPM estimate of how the team's shooting efficiency changes with the player on the floor, measured in percentage points. Teammates and opponents are accounted for, so it is not just the player's own shooting.
mpoTS%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means the team shoots more efficiently with the player on the floor.

mpdTS%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the opponents' true shooting % with the player on the floor, in points. Lower is better.
mpdTS%.glossary: The same estimate for the opponents' shooting efficiency. Negative values mean opponents shoot worse with the player on the floor.
mpdTS%.how_to_read: Lower is better. Negative means opponents shoot less efficiently against the player's team.

mpoTOV%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the team's turnover rate with the player on the floor, in points. Lower is better.
mpoTOV%.glossary: The one-year RAPM estimate of how the team's turnover rate changes with the player on the floor. Negative values mean fewer turnovers.
mpoTOV%.how_to_read: Lower is better. Negative means the team turns the ball over less with the player on the floor.

mpdTOV%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the opponents' turnover rate with the player on the floor, in points. Higher is better.
mpdTOV%.glossary: The same estimate for the opponents' turnover rate. Positive values mean the defense forces more turnovers with the player on the floor.
mpdTOV%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means opponents turn the ball over more.

mpoREB%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the team's offensive rebound rate with the player on the floor, in points. Higher is better.
mpoREB%.glossary: The one-year RAPM estimate of how the team's offensive rebounding changes with the player on the floor. Positive values mean more second chances.
mpoREB%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means the team grabs more of its own misses.

mpdREB%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the team's defensive rebound rate with the player on the floor, in points. Higher is better.
mpdREB%.glossary: The one-year RAPM estimate of how the team's defensive rebounding changes with the player on the floor. Positive values mean the team secures more of the opponents' misses.
mpdREB%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means the team finishes more defensive possessions with the rebound.

mpoFTr%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of how often the team gets to the free-throw line with the player on the floor. Higher is better.
mpoFTr%.glossary: The one-year RAPM estimate of how the team's rate of getting to the line changes with the player on the floor. Teammates and opponents are accounted for.
mpoFTr%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means the team gets to the line more with the player on the floor.

mpdFTr%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of how often opponents get to the free-throw line with the player on the floor. Lower is better.
mpdFTr%.glossary: The same estimate for the opponents' rate of getting to the line. Negative values mean the player's team sends opponents to the line less.
mpdFTr%.how_to_read: Lower is better. Negative means opponents get to the line less.

mpoAST%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the share of the team's made shots that are assisted. A style measure, not quality.
mpoAST%.glossary: The one-year RAPM estimate of how the share of the team's made shots that are assisted changes with the player on the floor. It describes ball movement: passers and players who finish off passes raise it, self-creators lower it.
mpoAST%.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it mostly describes style: more or less ball movement, not quality.

mpo3PAr%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the share of the team's shots that are threes. Describes style, not quality.
mpo3PAr%.glossary: The one-year RAPM estimate of how the share of the team's shots that are threes changes with the player on the floor. It shows the kind of shots a player shifts the offense toward, not how good they are. From 2002-03.
mpo3PAr%.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it mostly describes style: a more three-heavy shot mix.

mpoRIM%.tooltip: One-year RAPM of the share of the team's shots that are layups, dunks, tips or putbacks.
mpoRIM%.glossary: The one-year RAPM estimate of how the team's share of rim attempts changes with the player on the floor. It shows the kind of shots a player shifts the offense toward, not how good they are. From 2002-03.
mpoRIM%.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it mostly describes style: more shots at the rim.

OnNetRtg.tooltip: Team point margin per 100 possessions while the player is on court. Reflects teammates and opponents too.
OnNetRtg.how_to_read: Higher is better. It describes the lineups the player played in, not only the player.

OnOffNetRtg.tooltip: Team net rating on court minus off court, per 100 possessions. From Cleaning the Glass.
OnOffNetRtg.glossary: Team net rating with the player on the floor minus with the player off. Positive means the team does better with the player on. It is noisy and depends on who the backups are. From Cleaning the Glass, which removes garbage time. From 2003-04.
OnOffNetRtg.how_to_read: Higher is better. Treat it as context for the lineups the player played in, not a pure individual rating.

OnORtg.tooltip: Points the team scores per 100 possessions while the player is on court.
OnORtg.how_to_read: Higher is better. Team offense with the player on the floor.

OnOffORtg.tooltip: Team offensive rating on court minus off court, per 100 possessions. From Cleaning the Glass.
OnOffORtg.glossary: Positive means the team scores more per 100 possessions with the player on the floor than with the player on the bench.
OnOffORtg.how_to_read: Higher is better. A context stat; depends on the backups.

OnDRtg.tooltip: Points the team allows per 100 possessions while the player is on court.
OnDRtg.how_to_read: Lower is better. Team defense with the player on the floor.

OnOffDRtg.tooltip: Team defensive rating on court minus off court, per 100 possessions. From Cleaning the Glass.
OnOffDRtg.glossary: Negative means the team allows fewer points per 100 possessions with the player on the floor than with the player on the bench.
OnOffDRtg.how_to_read: Lower is better. A negative value means the team defends better with the player on.

OnOffDeFG%.tooltip: Change in opponents' eFG% with the player on vs off court, in points. From Cleaning the Glass.
OnOffDeFG%.glossary: Compares the effective field goal percentage opponents shoot with the player on the floor and off it. A negative value means opponents shoot worse with the player on.
OnOffDeFG%.how_to_read: Lower is better. Opponents shoot worse with the player on the floor.

OppRimFreq.tooltip: Share of the shots the player defended that came within 5 feet of the rim.
OppRimFreq.how_to_read: Lower is better (site ranking): fewer of the player's matchups get to the rim. Partly role: rim protectors are asked to defend more of these shots.

OnOffRimFreq.tooltip: Change in how often opponents shoot at the rim, player on vs off court. From Cleaning the Glass.
OnOffRimFreq.glossary: Compares the share of opponent shots taken at the rim with the player on the floor and off it. A negative value means opponents get to the rim less with the player on.
OnOffRimFreq.how_to_read: Lower is better. Fewer opponent shots at the rim with the player on the floor.

OnOffRimFG%.tooltip: Change in opponents' FG% at the rim, player on vs off court. From Cleaning the Glass.
OnOffRimFG%.glossary: Compares how often opponents make shots at the rim with the player on the floor and off it. A negative value means opponents finish worse at the rim with the player on.
OnOffRimFG%.how_to_read: Lower is better. Opponents finish worse at the rim with the player on the floor.

On_oSQ.tooltip: Average quality of the team's shots with the player on court, as an expected eFG%. Higher is better.
On_oSQ.glossary: Shot quality (SQ) rates every shot by how often an average shooter makes that kind of shot, so it measures how good the looks were, not whether they went in. On oSQ is the team's average while the player is on the floor.
On_oSQ.how_to_read: Higher is better. A higher value means the team gets better looks with the player on the floor.

OnOff_oSQ.tooltip: Change in the team's shot quality with the player on court vs off court. Higher is better.
OnOff_oSQ.glossary: The gap in the team's shot quality between the player's minutes on and off the floor. The player's own shots are included, so a player who gets great looks personally also scores well here.
OnOff_oSQ.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means the team gets better looks with the player on.

pOnOff_oSQ.tooltip: OnOff_oSQ steadied for small samples. Higher is better.
pOnOff_oSQ.glossary: The same on-off gap in team shot quality, adjusted so that players with few minutes are not pushed to the extremes by chance. Use it for comparing players with very different minutes.
pOnOff_oSQ.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means the team gets better looks with the player on.

On_dSQ.tooltip: Average quality of the shots opponents take with the player on court, as an expected eFG%. Lower is better.
On_dSQ.glossary: The average quality of the shots opponents take while the player is on the floor, using the same shot-quality idea as On oSQ. Lower means the defense gives up worse looks.
On_dSQ.how_to_read: Lower is better. Opponents get worse looks with the player on the floor.

OnOff_dSQ.tooltip: Change in opponents' shot quality with the player on court vs off court. Lower is better.
OnOff_dSQ.glossary: The gap in opponent shot quality between the player's minutes on and off the floor. Negative values mean opponents take worse shots with the player on.
OnOff_dSQ.how_to_read: Lower is better. Negative means opponents get worse looks with the player on.

pOnOff_dSQ.tooltip: OnOff_dSQ steadied for small samples, so thin minutes do not produce extreme values. Lower is better.
pOnOff_dSQ.glossary: The same on-off gap in opponent shot quality, adjusted so that players with few minutes are not pushed to the extremes by chance.
pOnOff_dSQ.how_to_read: Lower is better. Negative means opponents get worse looks with the player on.

OnTm_oSQ.tooltip: Quality of the shots the player's teammates take while the player is on court. Higher is better.
OnTm_oSQ.glossary: Shot quality for the teammates' shots only, with the player's own attempts left out. It shows how good the looks around the player are while the player is on the floor.
OnTm_oSQ.how_to_read: Higher is better. Teammates get better looks with the player on the floor.

WOWYTm_oSQ.tooltip: Do the same teammates get better shots with the player than without? Higher is better.
WOWYTm_oSQ.glossary: WOWY stands for with or without you: each teammate is compared with themselves in the two situations. The result shows how much the player changes the quality of teammates' looks.
WOWYTm_oSQ.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means teammates get better looks when the player is on the floor.

WOWYOnTmTS%.tooltip: Teammates' true shooting % with the player on court (same-teammate comparison). Higher is better.
WOWYOnTmTS%.glossary: How efficiently the player's teammates shoot with the player on the floor. It is team context: it reflects who the teammates are as well as the looks the player helps create.
WOWYOnTmTS%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Teammates shoot more efficiently with the player on the floor.

WOWYOnOffTmTS%.tooltip: Teammates' true shooting % with the player vs without, comparing the same teammates. Higher is better.
WOWYOnOffTmTS%.glossary: A with-or-without-you comparison: the same teammates' shooting efficiency when the player is on the floor and when the player is off it.
WOWYOnOffTmTS%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means teammates shoot better with the player on the floor.

pWOWYTmTS%.tooltip: WOWYTmTS% steadied for small samples, so thin minutes do not produce extreme values. Higher is better.
pWOWYTmTS%.glossary: The with-or-without-you gap in teammates' true shooting (the same teammates, with and without the player), padded so players with few minutes are not pushed to the extremes.
pWOWYTmTS%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means teammates shoot better with the player on the floor.

WOWYOnTm3PRate.tooltip: Share of teammates' shots that are threes while the player is on court.
WOWYOnTm3PRate.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it mostly describes shot style: a more three-heavy mix.

WOWYOnOffTm3PRate.tooltip: Change in teammates' three-point attempt share with the player vs without, same teammates.
WOWYOnOffTm3PRate.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it mostly describes shot style: more threes around the player.

WOWYOnTmRimRate.tooltip: Share of teammates' shots that are layups, dunks, tips or putbacks while the player is on court. From 2002-03.
WOWYOnTmRimRate.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it mostly describes shot style: more shots at the rim.

WOWYOnOffTmRimRate.tooltip: Change in teammates' share of layups, dunks, tips and putbacks with the player vs without, same teammates. From 2002-03.
WOWYOnOffTmRimRate.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it mostly describes shot style: more shots at the rim around the player.

TotalPoss.tooltip: Possessions the player was on court for, offense and defense combined.
TotalPoss.how_to_read: Volume and sample size, not quality; no good or bad direction.

PointsPerUsedPoss.tooltip: Points the player produces, scored or assisted, per possession they use as a scorer or creator. Higher is better.
PointsPerUsedPoss.glossary: Counts every possession the player finishes (shot, free throws, turnover) or sets up with a pass, and the points that came from them, the player's own plus those from assists. An efficiency measure over the whole workload. From 2013-14.
PointsPerUsedPoss.how_to_read: Higher is better. More points for every possession the player uses.

OffPoss.tooltip: Offensive possessions the player was on court for.
OffPoss.how_to_read: Volume and sample size, not quality; no good or bad direction.

DefPoss.tooltip: Defensive possessions the player was on court for.
DefPoss.how_to_read: Volume and sample size, not quality; no good or bad direction.

Load.tooltip: How many of every 100 team possessions the player is directly involved in, as a shooter or creator.
Load.glossary: Ben Taylor's estimate of how many of a team's possessions a player is directly involved in, by shooting, getting to the line, turning it over or setting up teammates. High values mark the focal points of an offense. Atlantic Hoops' implementation of Taylor's concept.
Load.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role measure: a heavy load with poor efficiency is not good.

BoxCreation.tooltip: Estimated shots the player creates for teammates per 100 possessions, from the box score.
BoxCreation.glossary: Ben Taylor's box-score estimate of how many shots a player creates for teammates every 100 possessions. High values mark players who set up offense for others. Atlantic Hoops' implementation of Taylor's concept.
BoxCreation.how_to_read: Higher is better. More shots created for teammates.

TotUSG%.tooltip: Total usage: how much of the team's offense runs through the player, as a finisher or as a passer who creates shots.
TotUSG%.glossary: Standard usage (USG%) only reflects the plays a player finishes. Total usage adds playmaking usage (PmUSG%), the chances the player creates for teammates, so a pass-first point guard's role is not undercounted. From 2013-14.
TotUSG%.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat: it shows offensive responsibility, not quality.

USG%.tooltip: Estimated share of team plays the player ends with a shot, free throws or a turnover while on court.
USG%.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat: high usage with poor efficiency is not good.

PmUSG%.tooltip: The share of the team's scoring chances, while the player is on the floor, that come off the player's passes.
PmUSG%.glossary: Playmaking usage: the share of the team's scoring chances while the player is on the floor that end in a teammate's shot or free throws off the player's pass. Added to USG% it gives TotUSG%. From 2013-14.
PmUSG%.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat: it shows offensive responsibility, not quality.

PmUSG/USG.tooltip: Balance between creating for teammates and finishing plays. Higher means more of a passer than a scorer.
PmUSG/USG.glossary: The balance between creating for others (PmUSG%) and finishing plays (USG%). Above 1 marks pass-first players; near 0 marks pure finishers.
PmUSG/USG.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it describes role (passer or scorer), not quality.

TouchesPer75.tooltip: Times the player gets the ball per 75 possessions.
TouchesPer75.glossary: A touch is any time the player has possession of the ball, tracked by NBA cameras from 2013-14 onward. Many touches mark a primary ball handler; fewer mark an off-ball role.
TouchesPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat: it shows how involved the player is, not quality.

TimePerTouch.tooltip: Average seconds the player holds the ball per touch.
TimePerTouch.glossary: Long touches usually mark ball handlers who create; short touches mark quick decision-makers and off-ball players. Tracked from 2013-14 onward.
TimePerTouch.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a style stat: long holds suit creators, short holds suit connectors.

PaintTouchesPer75.tooltip: Touches in the painted area per 75 possessions.
PaintTouchesPer75.glossary: A paint touch is a touch that starts inside the lane. High values mark interior involvement: bigs, post players and cutters.
PaintTouchesPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat: it shows interior involvement.

PosRelPaintTouchesPer75.tooltip: Paint touches per 75 compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelPaintTouchesPer75.glossary: The position-relative version of Paint Tch/75. Positive means more paint touches than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelPaintTouchesPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat: it shows interior involvement for the position.

TurnoversPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better, but volume rises with role, so read it next to usage.

AdjTOV%.tooltip: Turnover rate adjusted to the player's total usage (TotUSG%). Lower is better.
AdjTOV%.glossary: Turnovers adjusted to the player's total usage (TotUSG%: scoring plus playmaking), so heavy creators are not punished just for having the ball more. Read it next to TOV/75.
AdjTOV%.how_to_read: Lower is better. Fewer turnovers on this adjusted basis.

%LiveBallTOs.tooltip: Share of the player's turnovers that were live-ball turnovers.
%LiveBallTOs.glossary: A live-ball turnover keeps play going without a whistle, usually a steal. They are costlier because they often start a fast break for the opponent.
%LiveBallTOs.how_to_read: Lower is better. A lower share means fewer of the player's turnovers lead to easy opponent scoring chances.

ForcedTOsPer75.tooltip: Charges committed plus live-ball turnovers such as interceptions and pick pockets, per 75 possessions.
ForcedTOsPer75.glossary: Turnovers the defense forces: charges committed and live-ball turnovers where the defense takes the ball, such as interceptions and pick pockets. Part of this number reflects the defenses the player faced.
ForcedTOsPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better. Fewer turnovers forced by the defense.

UnforcedTOsPer75.tooltip: Offensive fouls other than charges, offensive goaltends, travels and out-of-bounds turnovers, per 75 possessions.
UnforcedTOsPer75.glossary: Unforced turnovers combine offensive fouls (other than charges), offensive goaltends, travels and turnovers out of bounds. The forced/unforced split is a crude approximation, based on how engaged the defense usually is in each type of turnover, not a judgment of any single play.
UnforcedTOsPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better. Fewer turnovers of the types the defense usually has little hand in.

LiveBallTOsPer75.glossary: A live-ball turnover keeps play going without a whistle, usually a steal. Dead-ball turnovers stop play, such as traveling or stepping out of bounds.
LiveBallTOsPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better. Live-ball turnovers are costlier because they often lead to fast breaks.

DeadBallTOsPer75.tooltip: Dead-ball turnovers per 75 possessions, such as travels and out of bounds.
DeadBallTOsPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better. Dead-ball turnovers stop play and give the opponent no fast break.

LostBallPer75.tooltip: Lost-ball turnovers per 75 possessions: stripped, losing it out of bounds or traveling.
LostBallPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better. Better ball security.

LostBall:Touches.tooltip: Lost-ball turnovers as a share of the player's touches.
LostBall:Touches.glossary: Lost-ball turnovers relative to how often the player has the ball. It adjusts ball security for how much the player handles it.
LostBall:Touches.how_to_read: Lower is better. Better ball security per touch.

PointsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more scoring volume. Says nothing about efficiency on its own.

TS%.tooltip: True shooting %: points per scoring attempt, counting twos, threes and free throws together.
TS%.how_to_read: Higher is better. The best single number for scoring efficiency.

rTS%.tooltip: True shooting % relative to the league average, in points. Higher is better.
rTS%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means more efficient than the league average.

ShotQualityAvg.tooltip: Average expected eFG% of the player's shots (pbpstats.com model): how likely they were to go in. Lower means harder shots.
ShotQualityAvg.glossary: Shot Quality rates the shots a player takes by how easy they usually are to make, whatever the outcome. A lower value means harder shots on average, so it reads as shot difficulty and partly reflects shot selection and role.
ShotQualityAvg.how_to_read: Lower is better (site ranking): harder shots on average. Read as shot difficulty; partly a shot-selection and role stat.

eFG%.tooltip: Effective FG%: field goal % with threes weighted 1.5 times because they are worth more.

eFG_Diff.tooltip: Actual eFG% minus the eFG% expected from the shots taken, in points. Positive means above expectation.
eFG_Diff.glossary: Shows whether the player made more or fewer shots than the quality of those shots predicts (the expectation is pbpstats.com's shot-quality model). Compare with Shot Quality, which rates the shots themselves.
eFG_Diff.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means making more than expected on the shots taken.

ShotMaking.tooltip: Points per shot above what an average shooter would score on the same kinds of shots. Higher is better.
ShotMaking.glossary: Shot Making separates shot selection from execution: how many more points per shot the player scores than an average shooter would on the same kinds of shots. Available from 2013-14.
ShotMaking.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means scoring more than an average shooter would on the same shots.

3PShotMaking.tooltip: Points per three-point attempt above what an average shooter would score on similar threes. Higher is better.
3PShotMaking.glossary: The three-point version of Shot Making: how much more or less the player makes than the typical outcome on the threes taken. Small samples can swing it.
3PShotMaking.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means making more threes than an average shooter would on similar looks.

RimAttemptsPer75.tooltip: Field goal attempts at the rim per 75 possessions.
RimAttemptsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more rim pressure. Partly a style stat; bigs and slashers take more.

AtRimPctAssisted.tooltip: Share of the player's made shots at the rim that were assisted.
AtRimPctAssisted.how_to_read: Lower is better (site ranking: more self-created), but it is mostly role: rim-running bigs are naturally highly assisted.

%Assisted2PM.tooltip: Share of the player's made two-pointers that were assisted.
%Assisted2PM.how_to_read: Lower is better (site ranking: more self-created), but it is mostly role and style.

3PAPer75.tooltip: Three-point attempts per 75 possessions, heaves left out.
3PAPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more three-point volume. Says nothing about accuracy.

NonHeave3P%.glossary: Heaves are very long, last-second shots that drag down a player's three-point percentage through no fault of their shooting. Removing them gives a fairer view of accuracy. The exact heave definition is the data source's.
NonHeave3P%.how_to_read: Higher is better. A fairer measure of three-point accuracy than raw 3P%.

%Assisted3PM.tooltip: Share of the player's made threes that were assisted.
%Assisted3PM.how_to_read: Lower is better (site ranking: more self-created), but it is mostly role: catch-and-shoot specialists are near 100% assisted.

FoulsDrawnPer75.tooltip: Personal fouls committed against the player per 75 possessions.
FoulsDrawnPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. Gets to the line and puts defenders in foul trouble.

FTShareOfPoints.tooltip: Share of the player's points that come from free throws.
FTShareOfPoints.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking: draws fouls), but it is mostly a scoring-style stat.

GuardedScore.tooltip: How much opponents put their best on-ball defenders on the player. Higher means tougher matchups.
GuardedScore.glossary: Guarded Score reflects how strong the defenders were who guarded the player, so it is high when opponents assign their best on-ball defenders. It describes the difficulty faced, not how well the player scored. Available from 2017-18.
GuardedScore.how_to_read: Higher is better: tougher defensive matchups faced. Context for the player's scoring numbers.

ScoringQuality.tooltip: Atlantic Hoops' overall scoring rating, 0 to 100: efficiency, scoring load and shot difficulty in one number. Higher is better.
ScoringQuality.glossary: Scoring Quality sums up a player's scoring in one 0-100 number. Efficiency matters most, with extra credit for staying efficient on a heavy scoring load and for taking and making hard shots.
ScoringQuality.how_to_read: Higher is better. Around 50 is the middle of the league.

DrivesPer75.tooltip: Drives to the basket per 75 possessions.
DrivesPer75.glossary: A drive is an off-the-dribble attack toward the basket in the half court, tracked by NBA cameras from 2013-14 onward. High values mark players who attack the rim from the perimeter.
DrivesPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more rim attacks off the dribble. A role and style stat as well as a skill.

PosAdjDriverPer75.tooltip: Drives per 75 possessions, compared with the average player at the same position.
PosAdjDriverPer75.glossary: The position-relative version of Drives/75. Positive means more drives than a typical player at the same position.
PosAdjDriverPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a style stat: how often the player attacks off the dribble for the position.

EstPPPperDrive.tooltip: Points per drive, counting the player's own points plus estimated points from assists on drives. Higher is better.
EstPPPperDrive.glossary: An estimate of all the scoring a player's drives produce: their own points plus the value of passes that lead to teammates' baskets.
EstPPPperDrive.how_to_read: Higher is better. More scoring generated per drive.

PointsPerDrive.tooltip: Points the player scores per drive.
PointsPerDrive.how_to_read: Higher is better. Better scoring and finishing on drives.

FGAPerDrive.tooltip: Share of drives that end in the player's own shot.
FGAPerDrive.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is mostly style: scorer or passer.

FG%onDrives.tooltip: Field goal % on shots taken off drives.
FG%onDrives.how_to_read: Higher is better. Better finishing on drives.

PassPerDrive.tooltip: Share of drives that end in a pass.
PassPerDrive.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): drives that create for teammates. Largely a style stat.

AssistsPerDrive.tooltip: Share of drives that end in an assist.
AssistsPerDrive.how_to_read: Higher is better. Drives that create made shots for teammates.

TOsPerDrive.tooltip: Share of drives that end in a turnover.
TOsPerDrive.how_to_read: Lower is better. Better ball security when attacking.

TOs:Pass.tooltip: Drive turnovers relative to drive passes. Lower is better.
TOs:Pass.glossary: Compares how often drives end in a turnover with how often they end in a pass. The lower the ratio, the safer the player is when attacking.
TOs:Pass.how_to_read: Lower is better. Safer decisions when attacking.

FoulsDrawnPerDrive.tooltip: Share of drives that draw a foul.
FoulsDrawnPerDrive.how_to_read: Higher is better. Drives that earn free throws.

FTAPerDrive.how_to_read: Higher is better. Drives that earn free throws.

PullUpsPer75.tooltip: Pull-up jump shot attempts per 75 possessions.
PullUpsPer75.glossary: A pull-up is a jump shot taken off the dribble, away from the basket. It is the hardest common jump shot, so even average accuracy is valuable. Tracked from 2013-14 onward.
PullUpsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more self-created shots. A role stat; accuracy is in the other pull-up columns.

PullUpeFG%.tooltip: Effective FG% on pull-up jump shots.

PullUp2sPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more self-created twos. Volume, not accuracy.

PullUp3sPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more self-created threes. Volume, not accuracy.

C&S3APer75.glossary: Catch-and-shoot means shooting right off a pass with a quick release and little or no dribbling. High values mark off-ball shooters.
C&S3APer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more off-ball shooting. A role stat; accuracy is in C&S 3P%.

RimFrequency.tooltip: Share of the player's shot attempts taken at the rim.
RimFrequency.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a style stat: a rim-heavy shot diet, generally efficient.

PosRelRimFrequency.tooltip: Rim frequency compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelRimFrequency.glossary: The position-relative version of Rim Freq. Positive means more shots at the rim than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelRimFrequency.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a style stat: how rim-heavy the shot diet is for the position.

RimFG%.tooltip: Field goal % on shots at the rim.
RimFG%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Better finishing at the rim.

PosRelRimFG%.tooltip: Rim FG% compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelRimFG%.glossary: The position-relative version of Rim FG%. Positive means finishing better at the rim than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelRimFG%.how_to_read: Higher is better. Better finishing than the position average.

ShortMidFrequency.tooltip: Share of attempts from short mid-range: floaters, hooks and short jumpers.
ShortMidFrequency.glossary: Short mid-range sits between the rim area and long mid-range and covers floaters, hooks and short jumpers. The data source defines the exact boundaries.
ShortMidFrequency.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a style stat: a floater and short-jumper shot diet.

ShortMidFG%.tooltip: Field goal % on short mid-range shots.

LongMidFrequency.tooltip: Share of attempts from long mid-range: two-point jumpers far from the rim.
LongMidFrequency.glossary: Long mid-range covers two-point jumpers beyond short mid-range, out to the three-point line. It is usually the least efficient shot.
LongMidFrequency.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but long twos are usually the least efficient shot, so a high share is not a plus on its own.

LongMidFG%.tooltip: Field goal % on long mid-range shots.

Corner3Frequency.tooltip: Share of the player's attempts that are corner threes.
Corner3Frequency.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat: spot-up wings take most corner threes.

Arc3Frequency.tooltip: Share of the player's attempts that are above-the-break threes.
Arc3Frequency.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a style stat: how much of the shot diet is non-corner threes.

3PRate.tooltip: Share of the player's field goal attempts that are threes.
3PRate.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a style stat: how three-heavy the shot diet is.

Predicted3P%.tooltip: Expected 3P% from the player's recent shooting and how closely guarded this season's threes were.
Predicted3P%.glossary: Pred 3P% asks: given how well this player has shot tight and open threes in recent seasons, what should they shoot on this season's mix? It is steadier than one season of 3P%. Compare with 3P% vs Pred. Blank when there is too little earlier three-point data. From 2015-16; not available for playoffs.
Predicted3P%.how_to_read: Higher is better. A higher expected three-point percentage.

3P%_Diff.tooltip: Actual three-point % minus predicted three-point %, in points. Positive means above expectation.
3P%_Diff.glossary: Shows whether the player is hitting more or fewer threes than their recent track record predicts. Big gaps often point to hot or cold streaks that may not last. Blank when there is too little earlier three-point data. Not available for playoffs.
3P%_Diff.how_to_read: Higher is better. Positive means shooting better than predicted.

%Tight3s.tooltip: Share of the player's threes taken with a defender within 4 feet.
%Tight3s.glossary: Threes taken with a defender within 4 feet (NBA tracking). A higher share usually means harder shots.
%Tight3s.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it mostly shows shot difficulty and style.

ShootingQuality.tooltip: How much and how well the player shoots threes, in one number. 0 is league average.
ShootingQuality.glossary: 3P Shooting Quality rewards the combination of three-point volume and accuracy, so neither a high-volume poor shooter nor a low-volume accurate one tops the list. It is measured against the league, with 0 as average.
ShootingQuality.how_to_read: Higher is better. Above 0 means a better three-point threat than the league average.

DietVersatility.tooltip: How evenly the player's shots are spread across the main shot zones. 0 is league average.
DietVersatility.glossary: A high value means the player scores from all over the floor rather than living in one zone. It describes variety, not efficiency.
DietVersatility.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a variety measure, not an efficiency one.

PosRelDV.tooltip: ShotDietVersatility compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelDV.glossary: The position-relative version of ShotDietVersatility. Positive means a more varied shot diet than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelDV.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a variety measure, not an efficiency one.

MoreyCoef.tooltip: Combined rim and three-point frequency: the share of the player's shots at the rim or from three.
MoreyCoef.glossary: Named after Daryl Morey, whose teams chased rim attempts and threes over mid-range jumpers. It is the player's combined rim and three-point frequency, from 0 to 1: 0.70 means 70% of the player's shots come at the rim or from three.
MoreyCoef.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): a shot diet closer to that ideal. It describes selection, not accuracy.

PassesPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is mostly a role and style stat, not quality.

AssistsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More playmaking volume.

AdjAssistsPer75.tooltip: Assists plus free-throw and secondary assists, per 75 possessions.
AdjAssistsPer75.glossary: NBA.com adjusted assists add free-throw assists and secondary assists to regular assists. This gives fuller credit for setting up scores.
AdjAssistsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. Fuller credit for creating scoring chances.

PotAssistsPer75.tooltip: Potential assists per 75 possessions: passes that lead to a shot, made or missed.
PotAssistsPer75.glossary: A potential assist is a pass to a teammate who shoots right after the catch, whether or not the shot goes in. It measures chance creation without teammates' shooting luck.
PotAssistsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More chances created for teammates.

RimAssistsPer75.tooltip: Assists on made shots at the rim per 75 possessions.
RimAssistsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. Rim assists set up the most valuable shots.

3PAssistsPer75.tooltip: Assists on made threes per 75 possessions.
3PAssistsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. Three-point assists set up high-value shots.

FTAssistsPer75.tooltip: Free-throw assists per 75 possessions: passes that lead to a shooting foul.
FTAssistsPer75.glossary: A free-throw assist is a pass to a teammate who is fouled in the act of shooting soon after the catch and goes to the line.
FTAssistsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More free throws created for teammates.

BadPassPer75.tooltip: Turnovers from bad passes per 75 possessions.
BadPassPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better, but it is naturally higher for high-volume passers.

Pass:Touch.tooltip: Passes per touch: how often the player moves the ball on after getting it.
Pass:Touch.glossary: A high value marks a facilitator who passes on most touches; a low value marks a finisher who keeps the ball.
Pass:Touch.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a style stat: facilitator or finisher.

PotAst:Pass.tooltip: Share of the player's passes that become potential assists.
PotAst:Pass.glossary: Shows how dangerous the player's passes are: how often a pass leads directly to a shot.
PotAst:Pass.how_to_read: Higher is better. Passes that create shots more often.

AdjAst:PotAst.tooltip: Adjusted assists as a share of potential assists: how often chances become credited assists.
AdjAst:PotAst.glossary: How often the chances the player creates become credited assists (free-throw and secondary assists included, so it can pass 100). It depends heavily on teammates' shooting.
AdjAst:PotAst.how_to_read: Higher is better, but it depends heavily on teammates' shooting.

BadPass:PotAst.tooltip: Bad-pass turnovers relative to potential assists: risk against reward. Lower is better.
BadPass:PotAst.glossary: Compares how often the player's passing costs a turnover with how many chances it creates. The lower the ratio, the more efficient the passer.
BadPass:PotAst.how_to_read: Lower is better. A careful, efficient passer.

PassTO:Pass.tooltip: Bad-pass turnovers as a share of the player's passes. Lower is better.
PassTO:Pass.glossary: The share of passes that end in a turnover. It adjusts passing mistakes for how much the player passes.
PassTO:Pass.how_to_read: Lower is better. A careful passer.

CreationVolume.tooltip: How many scoring chances the player creates with passes (potential assists), against the league. 0 is average.
CreationVolume.glossary: Measures passing volume: how often the player's passes lead straight to a teammate's shot, steadied for small samples and set against the league. Read it with the efficiency and playmaking columns. From 2013-14.
CreationVolume.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a volume and role measure, not quality.

PasserRating.tooltip: Passing skill on a 1 to 10 scale. After Ben Taylor (Thinking Basketball). Higher is a better passer.
PasserRating.glossary: Passer Rating is Ben Taylor's attempt to put one number on passing skill, rather than assist totals that depend on teammates' shooting. It runs from 1 to 10, with higher meaning a better passer. This is Atlantic Hoops' implementation of Ben Taylor's concept.
PasserRating.how_to_read: Higher is better. A higher rating means a better passer.

ScreenAssistsPer75.glossary: A screen assist is a screen that directly leads to a teammate's made field goal. It credits screen-setters, often bigs, for creating offense.
ScreenAssistsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More baskets created by screens.

PosRelScreenAst.tooltip: Screen assists per 75 compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelScreenAst.glossary: The position-relative version of Screen AST/75. Positive means more screen assists than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelScreenAst.how_to_read: Higher is better. More screen assists than the position average.

IndStopsPer75.tooltip: Steals, offensive fouls drawn and blocks the team recovers, per 75 possessions.
IndStopsPer75.glossary: Credits the player for personally ending opponent possessions: steals, offensive fouls drawn (charges included) and blocks the team recovers. A volume stat, so it favors active defenders.
IndStopsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More opponent possessions ended by the player.

MatchupScore.tooltip: Quality of the offensive players the player guards. Higher means tougher assignments.
MatchupScore.glossary: Matchup Score reflects who the player was assigned to guard: higher means stronger offensive players. It describes the assignment, not how well the player defended it. From 2017-18.
MatchupScore.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): tougher assignments. Context for the player's defensive numbers.

Chaos.tooltip: How much the player disrupts opponents (steals, deflections, charges) without fouling, on a 0-100 scale. Higher is better.
Chaos.glossary: Defensive Playmaking combines steals, deflections and charges drawn, and rewards doing it without fouling much. Rated 0 to 100 within the season. From 2015-16.
Chaos.how_to_read: Higher is better. More disruption of opposing possessions.

DTOVper75.tooltip: Turnovers the player's matchups commit per 75 possessions of guarding them.
DTOVper75.glossary: dTOV/75 counts the turnovers the player's assigned opponents commit while the player guards them. High values mark defenders who pressure ball handlers into mistakes.
DTOVper75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More turnovers forced on assigned opponents.

PosRelDTOV.tooltip: dTOV/75 compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelDTOV.glossary: The position-relative version of dTOV/75. Positive means forcing more turnovers than a typical defender at the same position.
PosRelDTOV.how_to_read: Higher is better. More turnovers forced than the position average.

FoulsPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better, though aggressive rim protectors foul more by role.

NetDCPer75.tooltip: Points the player's fouls and goaltends give away per 75 possessions, compared with the league average. Lower is better.
NetDCPer75.glossary: Net defensive cost: the points a player gives up through shooting fouls, goaltending and fouls in the bonus, against the league average. Below 0 means fouling costs the team less than average.
NetDCPer75.how_to_read: Lower is better. Below 0 means fewer points given away by fouling than the average player.

VersatilityRating.tooltip: How evenly the player's defensive assignments spread across the five positions. Higher means guarding a wider range.
VersatilityRating.glossary: A player who guards all five positions scores higher than one who guards mostly one. It describes the range of assignments, not how well they were defended.
VersatilityRating.how_to_read: Higher is better. A wider range of positions guarded.

PosRelVR.tooltip: Versatility Rating compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelVR.glossary: The position-relative version of Versatility Rtg. Positive means guarding a wider range than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelVR.how_to_read: Higher is better. A wider range than the position average.

LostBallStealsPer75.tooltip: Steals taken from a dribbler per 75 possessions.
LostBallStealsPer75.glossary: Pick pockets are steals where the defender takes the ball from a dribbler. Interceptions are steals of passes. The split shows whether a player's hands work on the ball or in the lanes.
LostBallStealsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More steals off the dribble.

InterceptionsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More passes picked off.

DeflectionsPer75.tooltip: Times the player gets a hand on the ball on a non-shot attempt, per 75 possessions.
DeflectionsPer75.glossary: A deflection is a defender touching the ball on a pass or dribble, short of a steal. It is a hustle stat from NBA tracking.
DeflectionsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More active hands and disruption.

ChargesDrawnPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. Each charge is a forced turnover.

OffensiveFoulsDrawnPer75.tooltip: Offensive fouls drawn per 75 possessions, including charges.
OffensiveFoulsDrawnPer75.glossary: Includes charges and other offensive fouls such as illegal screens. Each one is a forced turnover.
OffensiveFoulsDrawnPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More forced turnovers by drawing offensive fouls.

ContestedPer75.tooltip: Shots the player contested per 75 possessions.
ContestedPer75.glossary: A contest is a closeout with a hand up on a shot before release. It counts volume and effort, not whether the shot was stopped.
ContestedPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More activity contesting shots.

Contested2PsPer75.tooltip: Two-point shots the player contested per 75 possessions.
Contested2PsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More activity contesting twos.

Contested3PsPer75.tooltip: Three-point shots the player contested per 75 possessions.
Contested3PsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More activity contesting threes.

RecoveredBlocksPer75.tooltip: Blocks per 75 possessions after which the player's team got the ball.
RecoveredBlocksPer75.glossary: A recovered block ends the possession, while an unrecovered block can give the offense another chance.
RecoveredBlocksPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. Blocks that end the possession.

RecoveredBlocks%.tooltip: Share of the player's blocks that the player's team recovered.
RecoveredBlocks%.glossary: The share of blocks that end with the player's team getting the ball, rather than the offense keeping it.
RecoveredBlocks%.how_to_read: Higher is better. More blocks end the possession.

CostPerBlock.tooltip: Shooting fouls and goaltends committed for each block. Lower means cleaner shot blocking. Blank with no blocks.
CostPerBlock.glossary: Shows whether a shot blocker's blocks come with a lot of fouls and goaltends. A low value marks blocks that cost the team little. Blank for players with no blocks.
CostPerBlock.how_to_read: Lower is better. Unstable for players with very few blocks.

DFGA<6ftPer75.tooltip: Shots within 6 feet of the rim the player defends, per 75 possessions.
DFGA<6ftPer75.glossary: The NBA.com defense dashboard counts the shots at the rim that the player is defending. A high value marks a rim protector who is challenged often.
DFGA<6ftPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more rim shots challenged. A role stat as much as a skill.

DFG%<6ft.tooltip: Opponents' FG% on shots within 6 feet of the rim when the player defends them.
DFG%<6ft.how_to_read: Lower is better. Opponents finish worse at the rim against the player.

Diff%DFGA<6ft.tooltip: Opponents' FG% within 6 feet against the player minus their usual FG% there, in points. Lower is better.
Diff%DFGA<6ft.glossary: Negative values mean shooters do worse than normal against the player at the rim.
Diff%DFGA<6ft.how_to_read: Lower is better. A negative value means shooters do worse than usual against the player.

PointsSavedAtRim.tooltip: Points saved per 75 possessions on shots near the rim the player defends, after the cost of fouls. Higher is better.
PointsSavedAtRim.glossary: Compares how shooters do near the basket against the player with how they usually do, then subtracts the points given away by fouling. Per 75 possessions; Total PSR is the season total and Pos PSR compares with the position. From 2013-14.
PointsSavedAtRim.how_to_read: Higher is better. More points prevented at the rim.

PosAdjPSAR.tooltip: PTS Saved Rim compared with the average player at the same position.
PosAdjPSAR.glossary: PTS Saved Rim relative to the position average. Positive means saving more points at the rim than a typical player at the same position.
PosAdjPSAR.how_to_read: Higher is better. More points prevented than the position average.

TotalPSAR.tooltip: Total points saved at the rim over the season. Higher is better.
TotalPSAR.glossary: The season total of points saved at the rim. It grows with minutes and rim activity, so it favors high-volume rim defenders.
TotalPSAR.how_to_read: Higher is better. A larger total of points prevented at the rim.

ReboundsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better, though strongly tied to position.

O-ReboundsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better, though strongly tied to position.

D-ReboundsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better, though strongly tied to position.

AdjRebPer75.tooltip: Rebounds per 75 possessions, based on rebound chances rather than raw totals.
AdjRebPer75.glossary: Adjusted rebounding rates are tied to the rebound chances a player actually had, so they reward rebounds within the player's reach. Adj REB/75 combines the offensive and defensive versions.
AdjRebPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More rebounds won from the chances the player had.

ORebChancesPer75.glossary: A rebound chance is when the player is the closest to the ball from the time it drops below the rim until someone secures it. Tracked from 2013-14 onward.
ORebChancesPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more often in rebounding position. A role and positioning stat.

ORebChancesDeferedPer75.tooltip: Offensive rebound chances per 75 possessions where the player let a teammate take the ball.
ORebChancesDeferedPer75.glossary: A deferred chance is a rebound chance the player leaves to a teammate. It is a context stat and not clearly good or bad.
ORebChancesDeferedPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat and not clearly good or bad.

AdjOReb%OnChances.tooltip: Share of real offensive rebound chances the player secures, ignoring chances left to teammates.
AdjOReb%OnChances.glossary: Adjusted rebound percentage divides rebounds by the chances the player did not defer to a teammate. It shows how often the player wins the ball when it is really theirs to get.
AdjOReb%OnChances.how_to_read: Higher is better. A better conversion of real chances.

AdjORebPer75.tooltip: Offensive rebounds per 75 possessions, based on rebound chances rather than raw totals.
AdjORebPer75.glossary: The offensive half of Adj REB/75. It rewards offensive rebounds within the player's reach.
AdjORebPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More offensive rebounds won from the chances the player had.

DRebChancesPer75.glossary: A rebound chance is when the player is the closest to the ball from the time it drops below the rim until someone secures it.
DRebChancesPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): more often in rebounding position. A role and positioning stat.

DRebChancesDeferedPer75.tooltip: Defensive rebound chances per 75 possessions where the player let a teammate take the ball.
DRebChancesDeferedPer75.glossary: A deferred chance is a rebound chance the player leaves to a teammate. It is a context stat and not clearly good or bad.
DRebChancesDeferedPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat and not clearly good or bad.

AdjDReb%OnChances.tooltip: Share of real defensive rebound chances the player secures, ignoring chances left to teammates.
AdjDReb%OnChances.glossary: Adjusted rebound percentage divides rebounds by the chances the player did not defer to a teammate. It shows how often the player wins the ball when it is really theirs to get.
AdjDReb%OnChances.how_to_read: Higher is better. A better conversion of real chances.

AdjDRebPer75.tooltip: Defensive rebounds per 75 possessions, based on rebound chances rather than raw totals.
AdjDRebPer75.glossary: The defensive half of Adj REB/75. It rewards defensive rebounds within the player's reach.
AdjDRebPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More defensive rebounds won from the chances the player had.

%ContestedDReb.tooltip: Share of the player's defensive rebounds taken with an opponent close by.
%ContestedDReb.glossary: A contested rebound is one where an opponent is close to the rebounder. A high share means the player wins boards in traffic.
%ContestedDReb.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): wins rebounds in traffic. Partly a role stat.

%ContestedOReb.tooltip: Share of the player's offensive rebounds taken with an opponent close by.
%ContestedOReb.glossary: A contested rebound is one where an opponent is close to the rebounder. A high share means the player wins boards in traffic.
%ContestedOReb.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): wins rebounds in traffic. Partly a role stat.

%SelfOReb.tooltip: Share of the player's offensive rebounds that come off their own missed shots.
%SelfOReb.how_to_read: Lower is better (site ranking: more rebounds of teammates' misses). A context stat.

RebScore.tooltip: Overall rebounding rating against the league, offense and defense combined. 0 is average.
RebScore.glossary: Reb Score sums up a player's rebounding in one number against the league (0 = average). Each end is weighted by what a rebound there is worth. From 2013-14.
RebScore.how_to_read: Higher is better. Above 0 means better than the league-average rebounder.

PosRelRebScore.tooltip: Reb Score compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelRebScore.glossary: The position-relative version of Reb Score. Positive means rebounding better than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelRebScore.how_to_read: Higher is better. Better than the position average.

ORebScore.tooltip: Offensive rebounding rating against the league. 0 is average.
ORebScore.glossary: Offensive rebounding in one number against the league (0 = average). From 2013-14.
ORebScore.how_to_read: Higher is better. Above 0 means better than the league-average offensive rebounder.

PosRelORebScore.tooltip: OReb Score compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelORebScore.glossary: The position-relative version of OReb Score. Positive means offensive rebounding better than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelORebScore.how_to_read: Higher is better. Better than the position average.

DRebScore.tooltip: Defensive rebounding rating against the league. 0 is average.
DRebScore.glossary: Defensive rebounding in one number against the league (0 = average). From 2013-14.
DRebScore.how_to_read: Higher is better. Above 0 means better than the league-average defensive rebounder.

PosRelDRebScore.tooltip: DReb Score compared with the average player at the same position.
PosRelDRebScore.glossary: The position-relative version of DReb Score. Positive means defensive rebounding better than a typical player at the same position.
PosRelDRebScore.how_to_read: Higher is better. Better than the position average.

OffBoxOutsPer75.glossary: A box out is making contact with an opponent to keep them from the rebound. It is a hustle stat from NBA tracking and often explains why teammates rebound well.
OffBoxOutsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More opponents kept off the glass.

DefBoxOutsPer75.glossary: A box out is making contact with an opponent to keep them from the rebound. It is a hustle stat from NBA tracking and often explains why teammates rebound well.
DefBoxOutsPer75.how_to_read: Higher is better. More opponents kept off the glass.

FGA_Dunk.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): a total, so it mostly reflects volume and style.

PTS+/FGA_Dunk.tooltip: Points above average per dunk attempt.
PTS+/FGA_Dunk.glossary: Points per dunk attempt above or below the league average on dunks. Blank for players with fewer than 10 dunk attempts. Read it with Dunk PTS+ for the season total.
PTS+/FGA_Dunk.how_to_read: Higher is better. More points per dunk attempt than average.

PTS+_Dunk.tooltip: Season total of points above average on dunks.
PTS+_Dunk.glossary: Dunk PTS+ is the season total of points gained or lost on dunks compared with average. It grows with volume as well as efficiency.
PTS+_Dunk.how_to_read: Higher is better. More points added on dunks over the season.

FGA_Layup.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking): a total, so it mostly reflects volume and style.

PTS+/FGA_Layup.tooltip: Points above average per layup attempt.
PTS+/FGA_Layup.glossary: Points per layup attempt above or below the league average on layups. Blank for players with fewer than 10 layup attempts. Read it with Layup PTS+ for the season total.
PTS+/FGA_Layup.how_to_read: Higher is better. More points per layup attempt than average.

PTS+_Layup.tooltip: Season total of points above average on layups.
PTS+_Layup.glossary: Layup PTS+ is the season total of points gained or lost on layups compared with average. It grows with volume as well as efficiency.
PTS+_Layup.how_to_read: Higher is better. More points added on layups over the season.

POSS_PCT_Transition.tooltip: Share of the player's play-type possessions that are transition plays.
POSS_PCT_Transition.glossary: Transition plays end before the defense is set after a change of possession. Play types are assigned by the action that ends the possession.
POSS_PCT_Transition.how_to_read: Higher is better (site ranking), but it is a role stat: how often the player is used in this action, not quality.

PPP_Transition.tooltip: Points per possession on transition plays, including turnovers and free throws.
PPP_Transition.how_to_read: Higher is better. More points per possession in this action.

SCORE_Transition.tooltip: 0-100 rating of the player's volume-weighted points per possession on transition plays. Higher is better.
SCORE_Transition.glossary: Transition Score ranks players' efficiency on transition plays from 0 to 100, adjusted for the sample relative to the league, so it rewards being both effective and used. Compare with the raw Transition PPP.
SCORE_Transition.how_to_read: Higher is better. 50 is about the middle of the players listed for this play type.

OverallGravity.tooltip: How much defensive attention the player draws compared with what spacing predicts. 0 is league average.
OverallGravity.glossary: Gravity is NBA.com's measure of how much defenders shift toward a player compared with what the spacing predicts, measured in half-court sets. Shown here against the league, with 0 as average. Available from 2025-26 (NBA tracking).
OverallGravity.how_to_read: Higher is better. The defense bends toward the player, which opens space for teammates.

PerimeterGravity.tooltip: Gravity drawn on the perimeter, away from the basket. 0 is league average.
PerimeterGravity.glossary: The perimeter part of Gravity: the defensive attention the player draws far from the basket, whether with or without the ball. Available from 2025-26 (NBA tracking).
PerimeterGravity.how_to_read: Higher is better. More defensive attention drawn on the perimeter.

InteriorGravity.tooltip: Gravity drawn near the basket. 0 is league average.
InteriorGravity.glossary: The interior part of Gravity: the defensive attention the player draws close to the basket, whether with or without the ball. Available from 2025-26 (NBA tracking).
InteriorGravity.how_to_read: Higher is better. More defensive attention drawn near the basket.

OnBallGravity.tooltip: Gravity drawn while the player has the ball. 0 is league average.
OnBallGravity.glossary: The on-ball part of Gravity: the defensive attention the player draws while handling the ball. Available from 2025-26 (NBA tracking).
OnBallGravity.how_to_read: Higher is better. More defensive attention drawn with the ball.

OnPerGravity.tooltip: Gravity drawn on the perimeter while the player has the ball. 0 is league average.
OnPerGravity.glossary: The on-ball, perimeter split of Gravity: the attention the player draws when handling the ball away from the basket. Available from 2025-26 (NBA tracking).
OnPerGravity.how_to_read: Higher is better. More defensive attention drawn on the perimeter with the ball.

OnIntGravity.tooltip: Gravity drawn near the basket while the player has the ball. 0 is league average.
OnIntGravity.glossary: The on-ball, interior split of Gravity: the attention the player draws when handling the ball close to the basket. Available from 2025-26 (NBA tracking).
OnIntGravity.how_to_read: Higher is better. More defensive attention drawn near the basket with the ball.

OffPerGravity.tooltip: Gravity drawn on the perimeter while the player is off the ball. 0 is league average.
OffPerGravity.glossary: The off-ball, perimeter split of Gravity: the attention the player draws without the ball, such as spacing the floor as a shooter. Available from 2025-26 (NBA tracking).
OffPerGravity.how_to_read: Higher is better. More defensive attention drawn on the perimeter without the ball.

OffIntGravity.tooltip: Gravity drawn near the basket while the player is off the ball. 0 is league average.
OffIntGravity.glossary: The off-ball, interior split of Gravity: the attention the player draws without the ball close to the basket, such as rolling or cutting. Available from 2025-26 (NBA tracking).
OffIntGravity.how_to_read: Higher is better. More defensive attention drawn near the basket without the ball.

ShootingGravity.tooltip: The attention the player's shooting has drawn: tight shooting, shooting volume, spacing and movement scoring. 0 = league average.
ShootingGravity.glossary: A read on how much a player's shooting has pulled the defense toward them. It reflects how well the player shoots when closely guarded, how much the player shoots, the spacing that comes from being a threat away from the ball, and scoring that comes off movement. Atlantic Hoops' own measure, separate from NBA.com's Gravity. From 2013-14.
ShootingGravity.how_to_read: Higher means the player's shooting has drawn more defensive attention. 0 is league average.

MovementScoring.tooltip: How much the player scores off the ball: cuts, coming off screens and handoffs. 0 is league average.
MovementScoring.glossary: Mvmnt Scoring rewards players who run off-ball actions (cuts, coming off screens, handoffs) often and score well on them. Atlantic Hoops' own measure. From 2013-14.
MovementScoring.how_to_read: Higher is better. More scoring produced off movement.

Lineup Score.tooltip: Average Impact Aggregate of the player's teammates. Higher means stronger teammates.
Lineup Score.glossary: Lineup Quality shows the company a player keeps: how good the teammates around the player were, based on their Impact Aggregate. The offensive and defensive versions use O-Impact Aggregate and D-Impact Aggregate.
Lineup Score.how_to_read: Higher means better teammates. Context, not a measure of the player.

Lineup O-Score.tooltip: Average O-Impact Aggregate of the player's teammates. Higher means stronger offensive teammates.
Lineup O-Score.glossary: The offensive version of Lineup Quality: how good the player's teammates are on offense, based on their O-Impact Aggregate.
Lineup O-Score.how_to_read: Higher means better offensive teammates. Context, not a measure of the player.

Lineup D-Score.tooltip: Average D-Impact Aggregate of the player's teammates. Higher means stronger defensive teammates.
Lineup D-Score.glossary: The defensive version of Lineup Quality: how good the player's teammates are on defense, based on their D-Impact Aggregate.
Lineup D-Score.how_to_read: Higher means better defensive teammates. Context, not a measure of the player.

% Bad Lineups.tooltip: Share of the player's lineups that rate as bad.
% Bad Lineups.glossary: The share of the player's minutes spent with a bad supporting cast. Lineups are rated by how strong the teammates around the player are, from bad to elite.
% Bad Lineups.how_to_read: Context, not quality: more minutes with the weakest supporting casts.

% Mediocre Lineups.tooltip: Share of the player's lineups that rate as mediocre.
% Mediocre Lineups.glossary: The share of the player's minutes spent with a mediocre supporting cast. Lineups are rated by how strong the teammates around the player are, from bad to elite.
